reviewedFrom: EP14-05 (docs/enterprise-production/completion-checklist.json): imported and newly closed homes pass request, dispatch, visit, verification, dispute and recovery; coverage and accounting receipts reconcile. Builds on WARR-01 (EP11) and HOME-01 (warranty consumption, home controls). One builder (HOME-01's fixture): a home imported into the legacy Heron Bay community, and the Aspen-plan home on lot 1 of Cedar Ridge, $400,000, built ($72,000 land, $251,600 construction), completed July 1 with a $6,500 reserve and closed July 25 by the closing desk. A home released today cannot close in the past and a claim dated before its closing would book to work in progress, so the closed home is HOME-01's dated one; LOT-01 and SPEC-01 prove the lifecycle up to closing. Visits are recorded through the desktop service; the mobile visit flow (EP09-01) is out of scope.

imported-home-coverage-classifies-claims.derivation: Lot 7 of Heron Bay closed 2025-04-15 before Arc, sold with 12 months of workmanship, 24 of systems and 120 structural. The installed-base import enrolls it from that closing date: workmanship ended 2026-04-15, systems runs to 2027-04-15, structural to 2035-04-15, and the import's reconciliation counts one covered, active home with no exception. A grout claim under workmanship is out of warranty; a water-heater claim under systems is in warranty. No reserve was ever provided for a home that closed before Arc.

imported-home-request-to-recovery.derivation: A systems claim on the imported home: the warranty manager logs it (in warranty) and dispatches the technician; the technician records the visit as resolved and cannot verify their own work; the manager verifies it and the request is resolved. The plumber is backcharged $450 (callback $300, drying $150): issuing it books vendor credit WB-n of -$450; the plumber disputes; the manager settles for $300, so $150 is written off and reversal WB-n-R of +$150 is booked. The settlement is recorded as recovered ($300 collected, $150 given up) and its events read created, issued, disputed, resolved. The reversal waits as a pending payable until the owner approves it, and then posts. On the imported home the credit and its approved reversal net to -$300 of cost of sales (5000); the home has no reserve, so there is nothing to restore: no reserve balance and no recovery entry.

new-home-request-to-recovery.derivation: The home the closing desk closed on July 25 is enrolled by its closing, from the closing date, with the default program's terms. A systems claim (a supply line behind the sink) goes the same way as the imported home's: in warranty, dispatched to the technician, completed, refused to the technician's own verification, verified by the manager and resolved; the plumber's $450 backcharge is issued as vendor credit -$450, disputed and settled for $300 (recorded as recovered, $150 given up) with the $150 reversal (+$150) waiting as a pending payable until the owner approves it.

new-home-reserve-ties.derivation: The closing provided the $6,500 reserve. The framing crew's $600 repair bill, dated today, after the closing, posts to cost of sales (5000) and is approved against the verified visit: the reserve absorbs it (2260 debited $600, 5000 credited $600). The plumber's settled backcharge is a $450 credit less its approved $150 reversal, $300 off cost of sales, and the books restore the reserve for the $300 recovered once (Dr warranty costs 5050 $300, Cr reserve $300). From before the claim: 2260 +$600 - $300 = +$300 (reserve left $6,200), 5050 +$300, 5000 +$600 - $600 - $300 = -$300. One recovery entry. The land, completed-home, warranty-reserve and customer-deposit controls pass.
